Epitizide is implicated in targeting Tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 11A, which in turn is a target of 1-(4-acetyl-9H-pyrido[3,4-b]indol-8-yl)ethanone. This compound is likely acting as a modulator of the signaling pathways involving Tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 11A, which may influence the expression or activity of Platelet glycoprotein IX. The final score of 0.6656 indicates a moderate level of confidence in this pathway, suggesting that Epitizide may exert its effects through this intermediate target. However, the exact mechanism by which 1-(4-acetyl-9H-pyrido[3,4-b]indol-8-yl)ethanone influences Platelet glycoprotein IX remains to be fully elucidated. The evidence is consistent with a regulatory role of the identified compounds in the biological process, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the direct interaction between Epitizide and Platelet glycoprotein IX.
